summary: Ephemeral auth chaining + cross-tool idempotency mismatch causes duplicated downstream side-effects
description: Customer reports duplicated external side-effects (multiple webhook posts and duplicated DB writes) when using ephemeral API keys that are chained across long-running multi-tool calls. Pattern observed only when (1) client performs mid-request ephemeral key rotation/refresh, (2) a long-running function/tool call is in-flight, and (3) the SDK retries the request after a transient 5xx or connection drop. Customer uses a hybrid workflow: initial orchestration in TypeScript (serverless) then delegates to a Python worker to run a long tool chain that performs external webhooks and enqueues background jobs. They see duplicate downstream actions ~10-30% of the time during scale tests.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create an ephemeral API key with 30s TTL and configure SDK to auto-refresh via delegated token endpoint.
2) In TypeScript serverless, start a streaming chat that invokes two tools sequentially: (A) outbound webhook POST to third-party, (B) enqueue job to internal queueing service.
3) Hand off session metadata (ephemeral token + idempotency token) to a Python background worker that invokes the same Redwood function chain (tools executed in-process).
4) During the Python worker execution, simulate a transient backend 502 on the final acknowledgement (or close the socket mid-chunk) to trigger SDK retry behavior and a token refresh.
5) Observe whether the webhook receives duplicate POSTs and whether the queue service shows duplicate enqueued jobs.
6) Repeat with variable TTLs (15s, 30s, 60s) and with/without explicit per-tool idempotency keys.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: idempotency token scope is tied to ephemeral key lifetime; when token is reissued mid-flight the SDK normalizes the idempotency header differently between TS orchestration and Python worker leading to a mismatch on server-side dedupe.

Reproduced locally with a synthetic 502 injected into the last chunk. Observed that TypeScript client includes header 'X-Idemp: idt_12345' in handoff metadata, but the Python worker SDK re-encodes it as 'X-Idemp: idt_12345::ek_<new>' when it refreshes/attaches new ephemeral key. Server dedupe uses exact header match, so second replay is treated as distinct request.
Checked server logs: two distinct request IDs processed for the same logical operation within 500ms; dedupe keys did not match due to appended ephemeral key tag in the dedupe hashing path.

Edge-case: if the initial ephemeral key expires before the final ack, the runtime attaches 'auth-chain' baggage to outgoing tool calls; baggage serialization varies by SDK (python vs ts), causing inconsistent normalization across services.
Verified that disabling auto-attach of token metadata in the Python SDK avoided duplication (workaround), but this is not ideal for customers relying on seamless key rotation.

follow_up_actions: 1) Create INT ticket to align SDK idempotency header serialization across languages (python/ts/go).
2) Implement server-side fallback dedupe that canonicalizes idempotency keys by stripping ephemeral auth suffix for a short grace window (30s).
3) Ship patch to Python SDK to avoid appending ephemeral key to idempotency header when SDK performs implicit refresh; add opt-in behavior toggle.
4) Notify customer when workaround & patch lands and advise on short-term mitigations (explicit per-tool idempotency keys or disabling token auto-attach).
notes: Customer impact: duplicates of external webhook and queue writes leading to idempotency protection failures on third-party systems. Priority elevated given production-scale tests failing.
